sources.entry: What Makes a Great Product Manager

summary.title: What Makes a Great Product Manager
summary.one_liner: A 20-point list of behaviors the author has seen in the best product people, from starting with the customer's "why" to giving early, specific feedback.
keywords: what makes a good product manager
strong point of view weakly held
zoom in zoom out systems thinking
takeaways: Start with the customer and articulate clearly why someone would use the product and what problem it solves.
Invest in your strengths, prioritize ruthlessly, and be willing to cut features that do not improve the experience.
Hold a strong point of view but hold it weakly, changing course when evidence supports it.
Use data as one input, know when diminishing returns set in, and make decisions with incomplete information.
Share work early and often, and give feedback that is specific, useful, and kind.
summary.summary: The author, who has managed a couple hundred product and program managers, presents a personal, explicitly non-comprehensive list of 20 traits found in the best product people. The list is intentionally unordered, with the author naming three foundational traits: starting with why, curiosity, and a strong point of view held weakly. Each item is illustrated with a short anecdote and quotes from figures such as Jeff Bezos, Paul Graham, Pablo Picasso and Ben Horowitz. The piece frames the traits as skills over titles, applicable to designers, developers, marketers and sales people as well as product managers.
